questions.question: Explain forward current and reverse current in a diode. / [CO1]
questions.solution_html:
• Explain forward current and reverse current in a diode. [U] / [CO1]
  • A diode conducts current only when it is forward biased.
  • • Forward current: When the anode is positive w.r.t the cathode, the depletion layer
  • reduces and current flows easily.
  • • Reverse current: When the diode is reverse biased, only a very tiny leakage current
  • flows because the depletion region widens. If reverse voltage is too high,
  • breakdown may occur.

questions.question: What do you understand by avalanche breakdown? / [CO1]
questions.solution_html:
• What do you understand by avalanche breakdown? [K] / [CO1]
  • Avalanche breakdown occurs in a diode when high reverse voltage accelerates minority
  • carriers so fast that they collide with atoms and create more charge carriers.
  • This multiplication of carriers causes a sudden large reverse current.
  • Common in Zener diodes above 6 V.

questions.question: Explain the V-I Characteristics of JFET / [CO2]
questions.solution_html:
• Explain the V-I Characteristics of JFET. [U] / [CO2]
  • Introduction
  • A JFET (Junction Field Effect Transistor) is a voltage-controlled device where
  • current flows through a semiconductor channel.
  • Regions of V-I Characteristics
  • Ohmic (Linear) Region
  • • For small VDSVDS, the drain current IDID increases linearly with voltage.
  • • JFET behaves like a variable resistor.
  • Saturation (Pinch-off) Region
  • • After a certain voltage (pinch-off), current becomes constant.
  • • Controlled by gate voltage VGSVGS.
  • Cut-off Region
  • • If VGSVGS becomes more negative than cut-off voltage VGS(off)VGS(off),
  • ID=0ID=0
  • Effect of Gate Voltage
  • o More negative VGSVGS reduces channel width.
  • o Drain current equation:
  • ID=IDSS(1−VGSVGS(off))2ID=IDSS(1−VGS(off)VGS)2

questions.question: Explain the working principle of a half-wave rectifier and discuss its limitations and applications. / [CO2]
questions.solution_html:
• Explain the working principle of a half-wave rectifier and discuss its
  • limitations and applications. [U] / [CO2]
  • Working Principle
  • o Uses a single diode.
  • o During positive half cycle, diode becomes forward biased → passes current →
  • output obtained.
  • o During negative half cycle, diode becomes reverse biased → current blocked →
  • no output.
  • Waveform Behaviour
  • o Output is pulsating DC containing ripples.
  • Limitations
  • o Low efficiency (40.6%).
  • o High ripple factor (1.21).
  • o Not suitable for high-power applications.
  • o Utilizes only half of AC cycle.
  • Applications
  • o Signal demodulation (AM radios).
  • o Low-power DC supplies.
  • o Voltage multiplier circuits.
  • o Battery charging (simple circuits).

questions.question: What are the advantages of using a DPST switch over an SPST switch? [QNSMARTI:T:B20] / [CO3] [2x10 =20]
questions.solution_html:
• What are the advantages of using a DPST switch over an SPST switch?
  • SPST (Single Pole Single Throw) K/ [CO3]
  • o Controls only one circuit line.
  • o Turns ON/OFF a single conductor.
  • DPST (Double Pole Single Throw)
  • o Controls two separate lines simultaneously with one switch.
  • Advantages of DPST Over SPST
  • Better safety
  • • Disconnects both phase and neutral lines at the same time.
  • Controls two circuits together
  • • Useful for appliances requiring dual isolation.
  • Reduces risk of electric shock
  • • Full disconnection avoids accidental live contact.
  • Used in high-power devices
  • • Ensures complete cut off during servicing.
  • More reliable operation
  • • Prevents leakage or back feed from the second line.
